title: Blocks, transactions, and consensus
outcome: Explain what a miner proposes and what a full node verifies.
show: Draw three cards labeled user, miner, and full node. Connect them with arrows carrying a signed transaction, a candidate block, and an accepted or rejected result.
concepts: A Bitcoin transaction spends existing outputs and creates new outputs. The network checks signatures and spending rules.
A block links to a previous block and commits to a set of transactions. A node’s mempool holds pending transactions the node knows about. Different nodes can have different mempools.
Miners assemble candidate blocks and seek proof of work. Full nodes independently validate proof of work and the other consensus rules before accepting a block.
replicate: Write two sample payment slips and a duplicate that spends the same output.
Ask a partner to act as a full node and explain which conflicting spend is rejected after the first is included in the chosen chain.
check: Who decides whether a proposed block follows the rules?
Each full node checks independently against its consensus rules.

challenge.title: Send the records to the right place
challenge.prompt: Route each action to the role that performs it in this example.
cards: The wallet uses signing keys to authorize the transaction.
Build a candidate block and search for a qualifying hash
The miner assembles and hashes candidate headers.
Reject a candidate that contains a double spend
A full node checks the consensus rules independently.
Reject a block whose hash is above the required target
A full node validates the proof of work before accepting the block.
challenge.tip: Follow the record from signature to candidate to validation. One operator can run several roles.
